title: Arrive, Roppongi at night
anchor: The Louvre show at the National Art Center, open until 20:00 on Fridays.
notes: Land 14:45. The Skyliner reaches Keisei-Ueno in about 41 minutes; the hotel is a 10-minute walk.
17:00 Hibiya line from Naka-Okachimachi to Roppongi, no change, about 20 minutes.
17:20–18:00 Roppongi Hills Christmas Market, free, in its 20th year: Käthe Wohlfahrt ornaments, glühwein, sausages and stollen on the Ōyane Plaza. The Keyakizaka lights are on from 17:00.
Then the Louvre show from 18:15 (last entry 19:30). Leonardo's La Belle Ferronnière is in Japan for the first time and the show closes 13 Dec. ¥2,200 in advance.
Book 西麻布 豚組 for dinner: it is a Friday.
Mori Art Museum fits after dinner only if it is open late that night. One listing says it shuts at 17:00 on 27 Nov.
Not tonkatsu: Rojyu, a yakiniku top-100 that serves wagyu on large antique plates at Roppongi-itchome, can replace Butagumi. ¥15,000 course; its hours aren't confirmed yet.

title: Ginkgo, cats, Shimokita, Bazooka F
anchor: 神宮外苑いちょう並木 at 07:30, before the Saturday crush.
notes: 07:05 Ginza line from Suehirocho (G14) to Gaienmae (G03), no change, about 20 minutes.
Ginkgo first, Gotokuji second: the avenue is shoulder to shoulder by 11:00, the cats will still be there at 09:30.
To Gotokuji: Ginza line to Shibuya, Den-en-toshi line to Sangenjaya, then the Setagaya tram to Miyanosaka. About 40 minutes.

After Gotokuji: the Setagaya tram from Miyanosaka to Shoin-jinja-mae, a few stops back toward Sangenjaya, for SOUEN at 11:00, Sakurai's casual tea bar (walk-in, closed Wednesdays). Then the tram to Sangenjaya and a 20-minute walk up Chazawa-dōri to Shimokitazawa.

Shimokitazawa from 12:30: a curry top-100 lunch (Kyu Yamu-tei Shimokita-so, KALPASI or PANNYA; expect a queue), then vintage, then MATCHA PASSPORT at 14:15. Most shops open around noon and many take cash only. Keio Inokashira line to Shibuya at 15:10.
Shibuya Sky: a 15:30–16:00 slot gets daylight, sunset around 16:30, and the lights. Not booked yet: tickets have been on sale since 14 Nov and sunset slots sell out fast.
17:00 in Shibuya before dinner: Louis Vuitton Shibuya Men's holiday trains (free, to 31 Dec), Shibuya Loft, or coffee at Chatei Hatō or Kissa Satera.

Dinner booked: Bazooka F, Nishi-Shinjuku 7-15-5, at 19:45. Charcoal yakiniku; the signature is the Bazooka harami. JR Yamanote line from Shibuya to Shinjuku, about 7 minutes, then a 5–6 minute walk from the west exit.
Home: a nightcap at Omoide Yokochō first if you like, then the Oedo line from Shinjuku-nishiguchi straight to Ueno-okachimachi, near the hotel.

title: Todai ginkgo, then races or Kiyosumi
anchor: Japan Cup at 15:40 if the lottery comes through; MOT and Kiyosumi if not. Rikugien lit at night either way.
notes: Morning either way: Todai's ginkgo avenue to Yasuda Auditorium, quiet on a Sunday, then Kayaba Coffee 10 minutes' walk away.
Japan Cup: Shinjuku, then the Keio line to Fuchukeiba-seimonmae, about 35 minutes. In by 13:00 to see the paddock.
There is no gate sale on Japan Cup day. General admission lottery 22–24 Nov, result 25 Nov.
Clara's original afternoon: MOT's two shows, fukagawa-meshi (clams on rice) for lunch, Mameya Kakeru's coffee course, Kiyosumi Teien's stepping stones.
If the Japan Cup takes Sunday, MOT and Kiyosumi no longer move to Thursday: Thursday morning is now Tsukiji.
Rikugien: 18:00–20:30, last entry 19:30, ¥1,000 online or ¥1,200 cash. Then Tokiwa Shokudo, one stop away.
After Rikugien, instead of Tokiwa: Takokyu, a 14-seat oden counter in Yushima since 1904, open on Sundays. In winter arrive after 20:15; cash only; call 03-3831-5088 from 12:00 that day.

Plan B extras, all walk-in: Matcha& by Kiyosumi (amazake matcha, miso matcha latte). Kuramae is two stops away on the Oedo line: Kakimori's build-your-own notebooks (weekends 11:00–18:00), Pelican Café, Leaves Coffee Apartment. 2k540's makers, by the hotel, are open today too.
If the Japan Cup lottery fails: Chanel Nexus Hall in Ginza shows about 60 National Portrait Gallery photographs until today, free, 11:00–19:00. Tsukiji is shut today.

title: teamLab, Daikanyama, Yokohama
anchor: teamLab's first slot, the Dior Bamboo Pavilion at midday, then Yokohama's Christmas market at dusk.
notes: 08:00 Hibiya line from Naka-Okachimachi straight to Kamiyacho, about 20 minutes. teamLab is two minutes from exit 5.
Allow 1.5–2.5 hours. Check teamLab's calendar when booking: it closes some days without a fixed pattern.
11:15 Hibiya line from Kamiyacho to Naka-Meguro, direct, straight after teamLab. Onibus Coffee is a minute from the station; Daikanyama is about 10 minutes' walk up.

Daikanyama: lunch at Have More Curry (curry top 100), then the Dior Bamboo Pavilion (daily 11:00–19:00, walk-in; Café Dior needs an online booking by 23:00 the day before, not booked), then designer resale at Hedy and Eva Fashion Art. Monday hours for Hedy and Eva aren't checked.
14:45 Toyoko line from Daikanyama straight through to Bashamichi, about 40 minutes, in time for the 16:00 Air Cabin.
Monday is the market's calmest day, and the cable car catches sunset around 16:30.
Home: JR from Sakuragicho to Okachimachi or Akihabara, about 50 minutes.
Or dinner back near the hotel instead of Noge: Namaiki, a yakiniku top-100 two blocks away, open until 23:30.

title: Kamakura and Enoshima
anchor: Hasedera's maples and Enoshima on a weekday, then omakase at Ginza Ichibun at 18:00.
notes: 07:30 leave. JR to Tokyo, then the Yokosuka line to Kita-Kamakura, about an hour.
Kamakura's maples are among the last in Japan to turn, holding into early December.
Lunch: shirasu-don, whitebait on rice.
Enoden from Kamakura to Hase is five minutes; the Great Buddha is five minutes' walk from Hasedera.
Hasedera's night illumination, if it's announced, now clashes with the 18:00 dinner: keep the daytime order.
To dinner: Odakyu from Katase-Enoshima to Shinjuku, about 70 minutes, then the Marunouchi line to Ginza; or JR from Fujisawa to Tokyo. Leave Enoshima by about 16:15, before the sunset.

Dinner booked on Tabelog: Ginza Ichibun's omakase. Everyone starts together at 18:00, for about two hours; ¥28,600; no overly casual clothes. Afterwards walk 12 minutes to Ginza station, then the Ginza line from Ginza (G09) to Suehirocho (G14), no change.

title: Gyoen, Harajuku to Aoyama, a night out
anchor: Shinjuku Gyoen in the morning, designer resale from Harajuku to Aoyama, Sakurai's tea counter at 16:15, then racing or a hidden bar.
notes: Nezu Museum is closed between exhibitions from 24 Nov to 5 Dec, garden included. This day replaces it.
09:00 Marunouchi line from Awajicho straight to Shinjuku-gyoemmae. ¥500.

Optional, 11:00: BEAMS JAPAN in Shinjuku, five floors of made-in-Japan, about ten minutes' walk from the Gyoen's Shinjuku gate. Then the Fukutoshin line from Shinjuku-sanchome to Meiji-jingumae, two stops.
Lunch: Kaiten Sushi Ginza Onodera by Omotesando, about ¥300 a plate. Then Vintage Qoo before 14:00, Kindal, RAGTAG on Cat Street, and BEAMS and United Arrows in Jingumae 3-chome.

15:45 Koffee Mameya's standing bean counter, or Ippodo's Aoyama tearoom (optional booking). 16:15 Sakurai's eight-seat tea counter: not booked yet, book on TableCheck. The Teien Marimekko option drops.
After Sakurai: AURALEE's Aoyama store (12:00–20:00), then walk back down Omotesando under Fendi's 900,000 LEDs to evening A or B.
Evening A: Ōi night racing, ¥100, an SII race on the card, last race around 20:50, then Bar Trench. Pick this if the Japan Cup lottery fails.
Evening B: a top-100 sushi counter in Nakameguro, then Bar Benfiddich (TableCheck). Or Janai Coffee in Ebisu, or Gen Yamamoto.

More evenings: Kinju, a yakiniku top-100 in Nakameguro open until 03:30, fits Evening B; Nishio-san's Shizuoka oden in Shinjuku-sanchome goes before Benfiddich (same-day phone booking, cash). For a quiet night, Ishibashi's sukiyaki is a minute from Suehirocho (last order 20:00, cash only).

title: Tsukiji, the museum, Ginza, fly
anchor: Tsukiji's breakfast and market, the Daitoku-ji show, Ginza's brand spaces and Marunouchi's lights, then Narita for the 22:00 flight.
notes: 07:30 check out and leave the bags at the front desk; collect them at 17:30.

Tsukiji is open today (it shuts on 29 Nov and 2 Dec). Hibiya line from Naka-Okachimachi to Tsukiji, direct. Breakfast at Tsumugi in Tsukiji Hongwanji at 08:00: 16 small plates, rice porridge and miso, ¥2,200 with tea. Not booked yet: half of its 110 places a day are bookable online.
09:00 the outer market and Tsukiji Uogashi: tamagoyaki at Yamachō, a matcha whisk at Yamanoi Shōten. Eating while walking is banned: eat at the stall. Most shops close around 14:00.

The Daitoku-ji show is in its last week: Muqi's Dragon and Tiger and a National Treasure Ido tea bowl. Hibiya line from Tsukiji to Ueno, direct, for 10:15. Swap: Hamarikyu's teahouse instead, 10 minutes' walk from Tsukiji.
Sushi lunch in Ginza at 12:00, walk-in: Nemuro Hanamaru (Tokyu Plaza Ginza 10F; put your name down and wander) or Kaiten Toyama. Hibiya line from Ueno to Ginza, direct.

Afternoon in Ginza: Hermès Le Forum (Ann Veronica Janssens, free), Dover Street Market, Louis Vuitton's Le Café V, then tea and wagashi at HIGASHIYA GINZA at 15:00 and G.Itoya on the way to Marunouchi.
Naka-dōri's 1.2 km of lit trees come on at 16:00. Tokyo to Akihabara is four minutes.
Leave the hotel by 18:15 for Narita, 30 minutes earlier than before, for the tax-refund kiosk: Skyliner from Keisei-Ueno, about 41 minutes.
If the Japan Cup takes Sunday, Kuramae and 2k540 can go to Clara's morning on Fri 4 Dec.
